thread:
jordan: Quick Q — thinking about adding a damped eviction policy to reduce churn on busy GPUs. worried about interactions with KV warmup. could we repeatedly evict tenants and cause repeated warmups? cc @mira @sam

mira: Good callout. yes, naive damping can cause oscillation if warmup cost >> eviction benefit. we should gate eviction on both headroom and a KV-staleness signal.

sam: Agreed. my rough idea: only evict a tenant if both conditions are met:
```
1) last_active + damp_window < now
2) kv_local_hit_rate < hit_threshold
3) predicted_free_tokens > min_savings
```
That avoids evicting tenants who are inactive but have hot KV keys.
```

li-chen: Also consider a backoff counter per-tenant: each eviction increases a cooldown exponentially. prevents ping-pong with short reactivation.

jordan: Nice. what about cross-tenant warmup penalties? if we evict many tenants at once (e.g., after a traffic spike) we could overload the prefetch/warmup system.

mira: We can add a global warmup rate limiter and prioritize warmups by expected QPS. warmups for low-qps tenants get deprioritized. simple token-bucket on warmup jobs works.

sam: Implementation sketch for config options we can expose in the scheduler:
```
"eviction": {
  "damp_window_ms": 120000,
  "kv_hit_threshold": 0.15,
  "min_savings_tokens": 256,
  "cooldown_base_ms": 30000
},
"warmup": {
  "concurrency_limit": 8,
  "priority_policy": "qps_weighted",
  "global_rate_tokens_per_sec": 2048
}
```
These default numbers are totally heuristic.

li-chen: Tests we should run: microbench with simulated replays (short bursts causing mass eviction), measure warmup queue latencies, CPU/GPU load during warmups, and tail latency for reactivated tenants. Also chaos test: random evictions + warmup failures.

jordan: Sounds good. one more: observability. we need metrics: eviction_count, eviction_cooldowns, warmup_queue_length, warmup_throttle_drops, per-tenant warmup_time. Without that we won't be able to tune.

mira: Agreed. I'll add telemetry to the scheduler and warmup worker. runtime-bot will post a perf job after we land the feature.

runtime-bot: perf job queued: warmup-eviction-sim-3290001112. results ETA ~2h. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sam: Cool — i'll prototype the eviction gating logic and add unit tests for the cooldown/backoff. will grab the perf results and iterate.

jordan: Awesome — thanks team. if perf shows warmup storms, we can add a soft-fail mode that skips warmup for low-priority tenants (fast fallback to smaller model)
